summary: Cold read of the recorded assistant-exploration-view contract and task plan (Codex gpt-5.6-terra @ xhigh, read-only) returned NOT CONVERGED with four product decisions plus three closing notes. All were verified against the repository before being acted on and all held; three were defects in the contract the orchestrator had authored, the most consequential being that NOTHING in the frontend can create a saved view or a pin, which made task 3's routes unreachable and the approved plan's functional check unperformable. Three decisions went to the human in one round; the fourth - where an opened result renders - was resolved from the contract itself, which forbids a second renderer. write_scope rose from 13 paths to 20, required leaves from 6 to 7, and the review budget from 13/1800 to 20/2600. The task is no longer frontend-only: the shared label constant touches contract/src/api.ts and backend/src/semantic/semanticLayer.ts.

criteria_map.Saved-view labels come from ONE source t: Label source. The cold read found saved queries store only ids while the labels live solely in semanticLayer.ts:14-95, with no endpoint publishing them - GET /api/mis/options returns the four report selectors, not measures or dimensions - so the original criterion's 'derive from the registered catalog' was unachievable frontend-only. Verified before acting. The human chose ONE shared constant in @3f/contract that semanticLayer.ts imports, rejecting a static client copy explicitly because nothing would catch its drift, a backend display descriptor because it reopens a just-merged API, and a persisted label column because it needs a second migration and freezes stale text. The unavailable-definition fallback the grill also asked for is now defined.
criteria_map.Explore becomes a LIVE destination and t: Surfaces, and the pinned card's figure. The cold read confirmed app-shell.tsx:17 still renders 'Explore / Saved' with no href - the identical disabled-nav contradiction the task-2 grill caught for Ask - and that the dashboard is a placeholder. On the figure: the prototype draws pct and meta on each pinned card, but decision 0028 deleted every stored figure, so drawing one means a governed warehouse execution per pin on every dashboard load. The human chose metadata-only until an explicit Open, over re-running every pin on load and over a lazy viewport fan-out. The divergence from the prototype is deliberate and recorded in the criterion.
criteria_map.Opening RE-RUNS the stored selection and: The re-run path and where the result renders. The orchestrator verified before contracting that no backend work is needed: chat.controller.ts:38 passes a client selection through and chat.service.ts:162 assigns it directly, bypassing the model. The cold read then found the rendering gap the first draft missed: ask-panel.tsx exports only AskPanel and parseActiveBatchIds, and AskContextValue types ask as (question: string) => Promise<void>, so nothing could carry a selection and an inline render would duplicate the renderer. Resolved from the contract itself, which forbids a divergent second implementation: AskProvider gains a selection-bearing re-run and opening navigates to /ask. The two silent traps - reportGrounding winning over the selection, and the non-empty question requirement - are written into the criterion and reviewer focus.
criteria_map.A refusal renders AS a refusal, never as: Refusals. Unchanged in substance from the first draft and confirmed by the cold read: status is the REQUIRED discriminated union task 3 shipped, a non-runnable row shows its message and offers no open control, is never hidden and stays deletable, and a non-success ResponseClass renders through task 2's existing seven-class renderer. The orchestrator also corrected a wrong citation it had been carrying: decision 0018 is the unmapped-GL bucket record, not a record titled 'a zero is not an absence' - no such file exists. Its actual principle (an unresolved thing becomes a visible, distinctly-labelled outcome carrying its status rather than being excluded) does support the refusal rule, so the citation stands with the correct title and path.
criteria_map.Saved views and pins can be CREATED and: Creation and deletion. The cold read found the most consequential gap: there is NO frontend caller of POST /api/saved or POST /api/pins anywhere, so task 3's routes are unreachable from the product and the approved story plan's own functional check - save and re-open, pin and re-open - could not be performed as written. This is the same class of error the task-2 grill caught, a live check that could not execute. The human chose that task 4 owns visible Save and Pin controls on a successful answer, over seeding by API and over deferring self-serve creation. Delete is now required from both surfaces, with a failed delete surfacing its error.
criteria_map.The surfaces are proven by vitest leaves: Proof. Leaves rose from six to seven and now cover open and delete on BOTH surfaces rather than saved views alone, plus the Save and Pin controls and the unavailable-definition fallback. frontend/app/globals.css entered scope after the grill noted the contract had no CSS path at all - task 2's .ask-panel rules live there. The functional check is now actually performable, because the controls it exercises exist; without them it was an unrunnable promise.

current_flow: Tasks 1-3 shipped the governed assistant, both Ask surfaces, and the saved/pins persistence with re-authorization and a fail-closed audit. None of it is reachable for exploration: app-shell.tsx:17 renders 'Explore / Saved' with no href, frontend/app/(app)/dashboard/page.tsx is a placeholder, there is no frontend/src/features/exploration directory, api.ts exposes only ask() typed to question and priorTurns, and no frontend code calls POST /api/saved or POST /api/pins at all. So a user can ask a question and read an answer, but cannot save it, pin it, or ever see it again - the persistence layer task 3 built is live, audited, and completely unreachable.
new_abstractions: A shared vocabulary constant in @3f/contract that the backend semantic registry imports, making the published measure and dimension labels a single artifact both runtimes read rather than a server fact the client must mirror.
A re-run action on AskProvider that submits a stored selection instead of a question, which is the first time this client asks the governed path to execute something the user did not just type.
A deliberate, recorded divergence from the approved prototype: pinned cards carry no figure, because decision 0028 removed the only thing that could have supplied one cheaply.
gaps: Saved-view labels had no achievable source: SavedQuery carries no name, the labels exist only in backend/src/semantic/semanticLayer.ts, and GET /api/mis/options publishes the four report selectors rather than measures or dimensions - so the criterion's 'derive from the registered catalog' could not be met by a frontend-only task.

Nothing in the product can create a saved view or a pin: there is no frontend caller of POST /api/saved or POST /api/pins, so task 3's routes are unreachable and the approved story plan's functional check - save and re-open, pin and re-open - could not be performed.

An opened result had nowhere to render without duplicating the renderer: ask-panel.tsx exports only AskPanel and parseActiveBatchIds, and AskContextValue types ask as (question: string) => Promise<void>, so the Ask surface could neither accept a stored selection nor lend its response renderer.
The contract named no stylesheet at all, while task 2's .ask-panel rules live in frontend/app/globals.css, so two new surfaces had no path in which to be styled.
Delete and open were proven on saved views only, not on pinned reports, and no fallback was defined for a selection naming a definition the semantic layer no longer registers.
contradictions: The approved prototype draws a figure on every pinned card (p.pct, p.meta) while decision 0028 - and task 3's deletion of Pin.snapshot and Pin.lastRefresh - means no figure is stored anywhere, so honouring the prototype would require a governed warehouse execution per pin on every dashboard load.

The contract required rendering through task 2's existing renderer while the only export that can render a response is AskPanel itself, a whole surface with its own composer and chrome - so 'reuse the renderer' and 'render inline beneath the row' could not both be satisfied.
resolutions: HUMAN (kl-rahulanand) - the measure and dimension labels move into the shared @3f/contract package and backend/src/semantic/semanticLayer.ts imports them, so server and client read one constant. A static frontend copy was rejected because nothing would catch its drift; a backend display descriptor because it reopens the API task 3 just merged; a persisted label column because it needs a second migration and would freeze a renamed measure's old text forever. semanticLayer.financial.test.ts:21 asserts the exact label strings and must pass unchanged, which is the proof the move published nothing new.

HUMAN (kl-rahulanand) - task 4 owns visible Save and Pin controls on a successful Ask answer, over seeding by API and over deferring self-serve creation. Without them the story would ship read-only surfaces over dead routes and the plan's own live check would be unrunnable. Controls appear only on a success, since only a success carries a runnable selection.

HUMAN (kl-rahulanand) - pinned cards show metadata only until an explicit Open: title, definition-changed state and an Open control, no figure. Rejected: re-running every pin on dashboard load, and a lazy viewport-triggered fan-out. The divergence from the prototype is recorded in criterion t-aev-c2 rather than left as an apparent oversight.

REPO-ANSWERED - the opened result renders by extending AskProvider with a selection-bearing re-run and navigating to /ask, appending to the existing thread. The contract already forbids a second, divergent renderer, and inline rendering would require exactly that, so this needed no human. frontend/src/features/assistant/use-ask.ts and ask-panel.tsx enter write_scope as files the work mechanically implies.

REPO-ANSWERED - frontend/app/globals.css enters write_scope beside task 2's .ask-panel rules; the required leaves now cover open and delete on BOTH surfaces; and the unavailable-definition fallback is defined as rendering the unregistered id verbatim, marked unavailable, so the row stays identifiable and deletable.

ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED BEFORE CONTRACTING - the re-run needs no backend route despite POST /api/mis/run taking the four report selectors rather than a Selection: chat.controller.ts:38 passes the request's selection into the service and chat.service.ts:162 assigns it directly, bypassing the model. The two silent traps on that path - usesEditedSelection being Boolean(editedSelection && !groundedReport), and the non-empty question requirement at chat.constants.ts:2 - are written into t-aev-c3 and reviewer_focus.

ORCHESTRATOR-CORRECTED - criterion t-aev-c4 cited decision 0018 under the title 'a zero is not an absence', which is not its title and matches no file in docs/decisions. 0018 is 0018-mis-selection-unmapped-gl-bucket, whose principle - do not exclude the unresolved, surface it as a visible distinctly-labelled outcome - is the right authority for rendering a refusal as a refusal, so the citation was corrected rather than dropped.
open_items: Carried forward, non-blocking - no 3F office or plant location is recorded anywhere in docs/; ap-south-1 was chosen from the code's existing default plus decision 0003's India-residency line. Put to the human again at this grill and not taken up; decision 0027 should be amended if a real residency requirement exists.

Carried forward, non-blocking - the configured Bedrock model is mistral.mistral-large-3-675b-instruct, not a Claude model. Decision 0027 fixes provider and region, not model family, so this is compliant as written.

Non-blocking - pinned cards deliberately diverge from the approved prototype by showing no figure. Recorded in the criterion and in reviewer_focus so a reviewer comparing against the prototype does not read it as an omission.
Non-blocking - D-0040 stands: HelpService suggests an unregistered 'state' dimension, so a suggested chip can still answer not_supported on these surfaces.

rounds.question: **Where do saved-view labels come from?** `SavedQuery` stores only ids (`contract/src/api.ts:372` — no name). The human-readable labels ("Actual", "Budget", "GL code", "Month") exist only inside `backend/src/semantic/semanticLayer.ts`, and no endpoint publishes them — `GET /api/mis/options` returns the four report selectors, not measures or dimensions. So my criterion "derive labels from the registered catalog" is not achievable frontend-only. This is my error in the contract.

**Nothing can create a saved view or a pin.** I verified it: there are zero frontend callers of `POST /api/saved` or `POST /api/pins`. Task 2 left creation out, so the backend routes task 3 shipped are unreachable from the UI. My own functional check says "save a selection, reopen it from Explore, pin it" — that check cannot run as written. (This is the same mistake the task-2 grill caught: a live check that couldn't execute.) The approved story plan's verify section also requires "save and re-open, pin and re-open".
options: Task 4 owns Save and Pin controls (Recommended)
Seed via API, revise the promise
